description: Auto Scaling Groups must have notification configurations set up to send scaling event notifications (e.g., to an SNS topic) for launch, terminate, or failure events.

decisionPoints.description: Whether any scaling-event notification configuration is associated with the Auto Scaling group being assessed
Which scaling event types the notification configuration subscribes to (instance launch, instance terminate, launch failure, terminate failure, or only the test notification)
Whether the notification configuration names a destination notification topic
Whether the notification configuration, or the group it is attached to, is only determined by a value not known until deployment
How many notification configurations are associated with the group, and whether they agree on covering scaling events

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group is defined with the notification configuration property omitted entirely from its definition
requirements.rationale: Amazon SNS notifications for Auto Scaling groups are opt-in with no service-applied default, so an Auto Scaling group that omits the notification configuration property is created with no notification configuration and sends no launch, terminate, or failure event notifications.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration(s) and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide for notification defaults. The CloudFormation property reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md) describes NotificationConfigurations purely as a structure you supply to specify an SNS topic and notification types; it is optional and the docs state no implicit/default value that AWS substitutes when it is absent. The Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling user guide "Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html) says "You can configure your Auto Scaling group to notify you of important events" and that with Amazon SNS "You can only turn Amazon SNS notifications on or off" — i.e. notification delivery exists only where an administrator explicitly registers a topic and notification types (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR), as also shown in the PutNotificationConfiguration/Write-ASNotificationConfiguration examples. Nothing documents an on-by-default notification path for a group created without it. Therefore the deployed state of a group defined with the notification configuration omitted is "no notifications configured," which is exactly the state the rule prohibits; this is a documented absence of any default, not merely missing template text.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has one notification configuration that sends instance launch and instance terminate events to a notification topic
requirements.rationale: The group carries a notification configuration bound to an SNS topic that publishes autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH and autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE events, and the rule is satisfied by launch, terminate, or failure event notifications, so launch plus terminate coverage meets it.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether a notification configuration covering only launch and terminate (without the *_ERROR failure types) satisfies a rule phrased as "launch, terminate, or failure events". Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide on SNS notifications. The CFN reference (aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration) documents NotificationTypes as a list drawn from autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, TEST_NOTIFICATION, with TopicARN required — i.e. each notification configuration is an explicit pairing of chosen event types with an SNS topic, and any subset of the allowed types is valid. The user guide "Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" confirms EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH means successful instance launch and EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE means successful instance termination, with the _ERROR variants being the failed-launch/failed-termination (failure) events. There is no default notification configuration in play here: one is explicitly present and it targets an SNS topic, so the deployed group will in fact publish scaling event notifications. The rule requires notifications "for launch, terminate, or failure events" — a disjunction — so launch and terminate types alone are sufficient; the absence of the _ERROR failure types is not a breach of a rule that accepts any of the three categories. Nothing in this configuration is deployment-time unknown; the topic ARN reference is immaterial because the presence and event types of the configuration are visible.

requirements.description: A scaling-event notification configuration exists in the same template but is associated with a different Auto Scaling group than the one being assessed, which has none of its own
requirements.rationale: Notification configurations are scoped to a single named Auto Scaling group and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling applies no default notification configuration, so the assessed group — whose own NotificationConfigurations is absent — will run with no scaling event notifications regardless of the configuration attached to a different group.
requirements.evidence:
The verdict turns on (a) whether a notification configuration declared for one Auto Scaling group has any effect on another group, and (b) whether Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling applies any default notification configuration when none is declared.

Searched the CloudFormation Template Reference for "AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfigurations property". The reference page for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration describes it as "A structure that specifies an Amazon SNS notification configuration for the NotificationConfigurations property of the AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup resource" — i.e. the structure is a property of one specific group resource, with no cross-resource or template-wide scope. It is an optional property, and the reference documents no default value or implicit notification target; nothing in the service supplies notifications when the property is omitted.

Searched the API reference for "PutNotificationConfiguration Auto Scaling group notification SNS topic default". The API "Configures an Auto Scaling group to send notifications when specified events take place... This configuration overwrites any existing configuration," and the request is keyed on a single AutoScalingGroupName (limit of 10 SNS topics per Auto Scaling group). This confirms notification configurations are per-group state, not shared: a configuration bound to group A cannot deliver launch/terminate/failure notifications for group B.

Therefore the sibling notification configuration in the template is irrelevant to the group under assessment. The assessed group has no notification configuration of its own, no default is applied, and it will be deployed with scaling event notifications off. The rule is owed a finding. The value is fully known at analysis time (an absent property on a specific resource), so no deployment-time-unknown exception applies.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration whose only event type is the test notification
requirements.rationale: A notification configuration listing only `autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION` sends nothing but a one-off test message to the topic, so no launch, terminate, or launch/terminate-error scaling event is ever delivered.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether `autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION` delivers any of the scaling event notifications the rule requires (launch, terminate, or failure). Searched AWS docs for the AutoScaling notification types and the CloudFormation NotificationConfiguration property. The CloudFormation/CDK reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md, mirrored in the CDK property reference) enumerates the allowed values as `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH`, `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR`, `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE`, `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR`, and `autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION` — showing TEST_NOTIFICATION is a distinct type, not an umbrella. The CDK ScalingEvent enum reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/api/v2/docs/aws-cdk-lib.aws_autoscaling.ScalingEvent.html) documents each member's effect: INSTANCE_LAUNCH "Notify when an instance was launched", INSTANCE_TERMINATE "Notify when an instance was terminated", the *_ERROR members for failures, and TEST_NOTIFICATION simply "Send a test notification to the topic." NotificationTypes is an explicitly supplied list with no service-applied default that would add the operational types, so a group whose only listed type is TEST_NOTIFICATION receives no notification for any actual scaling event. The AWS reference example template for a scaled, load-balanced application likewise configures the four operational types and not TEST_NOTIFICATION. The protection the rule targets is therefore absent, and the rule should fire.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration whose only event types are the instance launch failure and instance terminate failure events
requirements.rationale: The group has an active notification configuration whose event types, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR and autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, are the documented failed-launch and failed-termination scaling events that the rule accepts, so scaling event notifications are in fact being delivered.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether the two failure-only event types count as the "launch, terminate, or failure events" the rule requires. Searched AWS docs for the Auto Scaling notification types and the CloudFormation NotificationConfiguration property. The Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide page "Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html) enumerates the supported events: autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH (successful instance launch), autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR (failed instance launch), autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE (successful instance termination), autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR (failed instance termination); the API reference for NotificationConfiguration lists the same set plus autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION. The configuration under review therefore uses two real, non-test scaling event types that AWS documents as the launch-failure and termination-failure notifications, each paired with a topic in a NotificationConfiguration on the group, so the service will actually publish scaling event notifications to SNS. The rule's wording is disjunctive — launch, terminate, OR failure events — so a configuration limited to the two failure events still satisfies it; no doc supports requiring the successful-launch or successful-terminate types in addition. Nothing here is deployment-time unknown, and no default is at issue because the notification configuration is explicitly present.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration that lists no event types at all, leaving the event type list empty
requirements.rationale: An empty event-type list subscribes the topic to no scaling events, so the group delivers no launch, terminate, or failure notifications — the documentation describes NotificationTypes as the explicit list of event types that send a notification and defines no default set when it is empty or omitted.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation and API reference docs for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration / NotificationTypes and for PutNotificationConfiguration. The CFN property reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md) states NotificationTypes is "A list of event types that send a notification" with allowed values autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, TEST_NOTIFICATION; Required: No, and it documents no default value or implicit "all events" behavior when the list is absent or empty. The underlying PutNotificationConfiguration API treats notification_types as the required enumeration of events that cause a notification to be sent (AWS SDK references), reinforcing that notifications flow only for the event types explicitly listed. Therefore an ASG whose notification configuration lists no event types ends up in a runtime state where the SNS topic receives no launch, terminate, or failure notifications — the protection the rule requires is absent, not merely untyped. The TopicARN being present does not change this, since delivery is keyed on the event-type list. Nothing here depends on a deployment-time-resolved value: the empty list is known at analysis time.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration in which the event type list is omitted entirely while a destination topic is given
requirements.rationale: A notification configuration with a topic but no event types subscribes the group to nothing — Auto Scaling applies no default event set, so no launch, terminate, or failure notification is ever sent.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation and Auto Scaling API references for the NotificationConfiguration/NotificationTypes property. The CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md) lists NotificationTypes as "Required: No", "Type: Array of String", and enumerates the allowed values (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, ..._LAUNCH_ERROR, ..._TERMINATE, ..._TERMINATE_ERROR, autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION). It documents no default value — there is no implied event set that Auto Scaling substitutes when the list is absent. The underlying service API, PutNotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/APIReference/API_PutNotificationConfiguration.html), treats NotificationTypes as Required: Yes and describes it as "the type of event that causes the notification to be sent", confirming that the event types are the sole determinant of which events produce a message; nothing in the docs indicates a fallback to all types. The CloudFormation quickref also states notifications are sent "when the events specified by NotificationTypes occur", i.e. the list drives delivery. Therefore a configuration that names a destination topic but omits the event type list results in a group that emits no scaling event notification for launch, terminate, or failure events — the protection the rule requires is absent in the deployed state, not merely unwritten. This is the state the service will actually have, so the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration whose event type is a string that is not one of the recognized Auto Scaling event type values
requirements.rationale: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling only sends SNS notifications for the four documented event types (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR), so a notification configuration whose event type is some other string delivers no launch, terminate, or failure notification and leaves the group effectively unmonitored.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether a notification configuration carrying an event-type string outside the recognized set still yields the launch/terminate/failure notifications the rule requires. Searched the API reference for PutNotificationConfiguration and the CloudFormation NotificationConfiguration property: both define NotificationTypes only as an array of strings with a length/character pattern and explicitly defer the allowed values to DescribeAutoScalingNotificationTypes ("To query the notification types supported by Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, call the DescribeAutoScalingNotificationTypes API"), i.e. the schema itself does not constrain the string, so an arbitrary value is syntactically shaped like a valid one but is not a supported type. Searched the Auto Scaling User Guide for the supported set: "Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" enumerates exhaustively the events for which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling supports sending SNS notifications — autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH (successful launch), autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR (failed launch), autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE (successful termination), autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR (failed termination). The CloudFormation walkthrough example uses exactly these four values. There is no documented default or fallback event type applied when an unrecognized value is supplied, and no documented behaviour by which a non-listed string would produce launch, terminate, or failure messages. Consequently the resource ends up with a notification configuration that cannot fire for any of the events the rule targets — functionally equivalent to having no scaling-event notification. This is a concrete, analysis-time-known string, not a deploy-time-resolved input, so the intrinsic exception does not apply. Flagged on the documented enumeration of supported notification types.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration that subscribes to every supported event type, including launch, terminate, both failure events, and the test notification
requirements.rationale: The group declares a notification configuration with an SNS TopicARN covering all five supported event types (EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, TEST_NOTIFICATION), so scaling launch, terminate, and failure events are all delivered as the rule requires.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration. The docs state NotificationTypes is "A list of event types that send a notification" with allowed values exactly autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION, and TopicARN (the SNS topic) is required within the configuration. DescribeAutoScalingNotificationTypes output confirms these five are the complete supported set. The configuration under review subscribes to every one of them, including both failure (_ERROR) types, on an SNS topic — the maximal compliant state for this rule. There is no default involved: notifications are explicitly configured. Nothing in the docs suggests including TEST_NOTIFICATION or extra types weakens delivery of launch/terminate/failure events. Therefore the rule has nothing to flag.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration covering instance launch and terminate events in which the destination topic identifier is an empty value
requirements.rationale: A notification configuration whose destination topic identifier is empty names no SNS topic to publish to, so no launch, terminate, or failure notification can be delivered and the group is effectively without notifications.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration and the Auto Scaling PutNotificationConfiguration API. The CloudFormation property reference (aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration) documents `TopicARN` as "The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon SNS topic", Required: Yes — there is no default and no service-supplied fallback destination; NotificationTypes is the optional half of the pair. The Auto Scaling API docs for PutNotificationConfiguration likewise describe the operation as configuring the group to send notifications to a specified topic whose subscribers receive the event messages. An empty string is not an SNS topic ARN, so the configuration declares the desired event types (instance launch and terminate) while supplying no deliverable destination: nothing publishes anywhere, and the rule's requirement that scaling events be sent to an SNS topic is unmet. The empty value is present in the template and known at analysis time, so this is not a deployment-time unknown; and no possible reading of an empty topic identifier yields a valid delivery target, so the outcome is unambiguous. Judged on the documented requirement for a real topic ARN rather than on a missing default.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's notification configuration event types come entirely from a deployment-time input whose value cannot be resolved during analysis
requirements.rationale: The notification event types are supplied by a deployment-time input, so the scanner cannot know which types the group will actually subscribe to, and since valid resolved values include the launch/terminate/failure types the rule requires, no breach can be asserted at analysis time.
requirements.evidence: What the verdict turns on: whether a notification configuration whose NotificationTypes list is entirely a deployment-time input (e.g. a CloudFormation parameter / Ref) can be judged compliant or non-compliant before deployment. Searched the CloudFormation template reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md): the structure takes NotificationTypes (a list of event types) plus TopicARN, and there is no service-applied default set of event types documented — the value that matters is exactly the one supplied. Searched the Auto Scaling user guide / API reference for the permitted event types (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html and API_NotificationConfiguration): the accepted values are autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR and autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION. Four of the five accepted values are precisely the launch/terminate/failure events this rule demands, so a resolved input can readily satisfy the rule; it is not the case that every possible value breaches it (only a list consisting solely of TEST_NOTIFICATION would). Because the deciding value is unresolvable at analysis time and its outcome is genuinely ambiguous rather than uniformly non-compliant, the scanner cannot assert a breach: this is the deployment-time-input exception, so the rule owes no finding here.

requirements.description: Whether the Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration at all is controlled by a deployment-time condition that cannot be resolved during analysis
requirements.rationale: Whether the group ends up with a notification configuration depends on a condition resolved only at deployment time, so the scanner cannot know which of the two possible outcomes (notifications present, or absent) the resource will have, and one of them complies.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfigurations and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide for SNS notification behavior. The docs (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html) confirm NotificationConfigurations is optional and that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling sends SNS notifications for EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE and EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR only when a notification configuration is explicitly created — there is no implicit default notification target. So an omitted notification configuration would breach the rule. However, in this configuration the presence of the notification configuration is gated by a deployment-time condition/parameter that cannot be resolved during static analysis: if the condition evaluates true the group is deployed with a compliant notification configuration, if false it is not. Because not every possible resolution breaches the rule, the deployed state is genuinely unknown at analysis time and the scanner cannot assert a breach; this is the deployment-time-unknown exception, so the rule owes no finding here.

requirements.description: The Auto Scaling group that a scaling-event notification configuration applies to is supplied by a deployment-time input that cannot be resolved during analysis
requirements.rationale: The notification configuration's target group name comes from a deployment-time input, so the scanner cannot tell which Auto Scaling group the launch/terminate/failure notifications attach to and therefore cannot establish that any group lacks them.
requirements.evidence:
The rule asks whether an Auto Scaling group has notification configurations for launch, terminate, or failure events. In this configuration a standalone scaling-event notification configuration exists, but the Auto Scaling group it applies to is supplied by a deployment-time input (e.g. a template parameter or otherwise unresolvable reference) rather than a literal name or an in-template reference.

I checked how the association is expressed. The EC2 Auto Scaling API reference for NotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/APIReference/API_NotificationConfiguration.html) shows the record is a triple of AutoScalingGroupName, NotificationType (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, TEST_NOTIFICATION) and TopicARN — i.e. the binding between the notification and the group is carried entirely by the group name string. The CloudFormation reference for NotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.html) and the SNS notification options page (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html) confirm the same event types and that the notification is scoped to one named group; there is no service default that attaches a notification configuration to a group, and no default that makes an unnamed configuration apply to all groups.

Consequently the value that decides the verdict — which group this notification covers — is only known at deployment time. The notification itself is present and configured for the relevant event types, so it is not the case that every possible value of the input breaches the rule; whichever group name is supplied, that group receives launch/terminate/failure notifications. The scanner cannot assert that any specific Auto Scaling group is left without notifications, so it must not emit a finding. This is a genuine analysis-time unknown, not a merely absent value.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has an empty collection of notification configurations declared, containing no entries
requirements.rationale: An empty notification-configuration collection leaves the group with no SNS notification targets, and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling sends scaling notifications only for notification types explicitly configured — there is no default subscription — so no launch, terminate, or failure event is ever published.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfigurations and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide for SNS notification behavior. The CFN reference (aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration) describes NotificationConfigurations as an optional list where each entry supplies a TopicArn plus the NotificationTypes to publish; nothing in the reference indicates any implicit or default entry. The user guide topic "Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" states that you configure your group to notify you and that "You can only turn Amazon SNS notifications on or off," i.e. notifications are strictly opt-in per notification type (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR). Because the declared collection contains no entries, the deployed group has zero notification configurations — functionally identical to omitting the property — and the service applies no default topic or notification type. The value is fully known at analysis time (an empty literal list), so no deployment-time-unknown exception applies. The rule requires notification configurations for launch, terminate, or failure events; this configuration provides none, so the rule should fire.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has two notification configurations, one limited to the test notification event and another covering instance launch and terminate events, each with its own destination topic
requirements.rationale: One of the group's notification configurations subscribes an SNS topic to autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH and autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, so scaling event notifications are actually delivered, and the presence of an additional test-only configuration alongside it does not remove that coverage.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether the set of NotificationConfigurations on the Auto Scaling group includes at least one entry whose NotificationTypes cover a launch, terminate, or failure event with a destination topic — and whether a second, narrower configuration (TEST_NOTIFICATION only) undermines that.

Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration and the EC2 Auto Scaling API reference for PutNotificationConfiguration. The CFN NotificationConfiguration property page enumerates the allowed NotificationTypes as autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, and autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION, with TopicARN required. NotificationConfigurations is a list, and PutNotificationConfiguration confirms each configuration is an independent (notification types, topic) pairing — the service sends a notification to a topic for each event type listed in the configuration that names it. There is no interaction whereby one configuration suppresses another; a TEST_NOTIFICATION-only configuration simply adds a test-event subscription on its own topic.

Applying that here: the group carries two configurations, and one of them explicitly lists instance launch and instance terminate events with its own topic ARN. That is exactly the state the rule demands — real scaling event notifications (launch and terminate) are delivered to an SNS topic. The rule is phrased disjunctively ("launch, terminate, or failure events"), so covering launch and terminate satisfies it even though the failure/error types (EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR) are not listed. The second configuration being limited to autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION is not a breach; it is an extra, non-scaling subscription and the documented allowed-values list treats it as a legitimate type. No value here is deployment-time unknown; the notification types are literal.

Therefore the resource ends up in the compliant state and the rule owes it nothing.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has two notification configurations, both limited to the test notification event only, each pointing at a different destination topic
requirements.rationale: Both notification configurations subscribe only to autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION, which AWS documents as a configuration-verification notification and not one of the four scaling events (EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR), so no launch, terminate, or failure event will ever be delivered to either topic.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION counts as a launch/terminate/failure scaling event notification, and on whether having two configurations (even to different topics) changes that. Searched the AWS CLI/API reference for the notification type enumeration: describe-auto-scaling-notification-types and the NotificationConfiguration API/CloudFormation reference both list exactly five allowed values — autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, and TEST_NOTIFICATION. Read the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide page "Amazon SNS notification options for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" (redirected to ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html). Its "SNS notifications" section enumerates the events for which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling sends notifications, and the table contains only the four instance events (successful launch, failed launch, successful termination, failed termination). TEST_NOTIFICATION is not in that table; it appears in the guide only in the separate "Test the notification" workflow, i.e. it exists to verify that the topic/subscription plumbing works, not to report any scaling activity. Consequently a group whose only subscribed type is TEST_NOTIFICATION will emit nothing on instance launch, termination, or launch/termination failure. There is no default at play here: NotificationTypes is explicitly configured, and the configured value is the non-qualifying one, so no absent-value default needs to be looked up. The presence of two configurations pointing at different topics adds no coverage, since neither includes a qualifying type — the union of subscribed types is still {TEST_NOTIFICATION}. Nothing about this configuration is deployment-time unknown; the types are literal. Therefore the rule's requirement (notifications for launch, terminate, or failure events) is unmet and the rule should fire.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a notification configuration listing instance launch and instance terminate event types with no destination notification topic named at all
requirements.rationale: A notification configuration that names launch and terminate event types but no SNS topic has no delivery destination, so no scaling event notification is ever sent — TopicARN is a required part of the configuration and the service applies no default topic.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation template reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration and the autoscaling PutNotificationConfiguration API. The CFN property reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md) documents `NotificationTypes` as "Required: No" (allowed values include autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, the corresponding *_ERROR types, and TEST_NOTIFICATION) and `TopicARN` as "Required: Yes" — the topic ARN is the destination and there is no documented default or implicit topic the service substitutes when it is absent. The underlying API confirms this: PutNotificationConfiguration marks both TopicARN and NotificationTypes as REQUIRED, and describes the feature as sending notifications to subscribers of "the specified topic". So the configuration as described — event types listed, no destination topic named at all — cannot result in any notification being delivered for launch, terminate, or failure events; the state the service ends up in is "no scaling event notifications delivered", which is exactly what the rule forbids. This is not an absent-value-with-a-safe-default case and not a deploy-time unknown (no input parameter supplies the topic), so it is decided on the merits by the cited documentation.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has two notification configurations, one covering instance launch and the other covering instance terminate events, each with its own destination topic
requirements.rationale: The group already publishes scaling events to SNS — one configuration for instance launch and one for instance terminate, each with a valid topic ARN — which is exactly the launch/terminate/failure coverage the rule asks for, and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling supports multiple notification configurations each targeting its own topic.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether notification coverage split across two NotificationConfigurations entries (launch in one, terminate in the other, different topics) satisfies a rule that asks for notifications on launch, terminate, or failure events, and whether the service honours more than one such configuration.

Searched CloudFormation reference for "AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfigurations NotificationTypes" and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide for the SNS notification types. Findings: (1) https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.md documents NotificationConfigurations as a list of NotificationConfiguration structures, each pairing a TopicARN with a list of NotificationTypes — so multiple entries with distinct topics are the documented shape, not an error; the underlying API (PutNotificationConfiguration, shown in the PowerShell Write-ASNotificationConfiguration reference) is likewise per-topic. (2) https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html enumerates the supported event types: autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH (successful launch), EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR (failed launch), EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE (successful termination), EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR (failed termination).

Applying that: the resource as described has notification configurations present and non-empty, subscribing to instance launch and instance terminate events with topic destinations. The rule's requirement is disjunctive ("launch, terminate, or failure events"), so covering launch and terminate meets it; the absence of the *_ERROR types is not required by the rule's wording. No default is in play here because the setting is explicitly configured — the deployed group will emit SNS notifications on both scaling directions. Therefore the rule owes this configuration nothing: pass.

requirements.description: An Auto Scaling group with a scaling-event notification configuration whose destination SNS topic comes from a deployment-time input that cannot be resolved during analysis, while the configuration's event types are stated literally as only the Auto Scaling test notification event, with no instance-launch, instance-terminate, launch-error, or terminate-error event type included.
requirements.rationale: The notification configuration's only event type is autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION, which AWS documents as a test-only notification distinct from the EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR and EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR types, so no scaling launch, terminate, or failure event is ever delivered regardless of which SNS topic the deployment-time input resolves to.
requirements.evidence:
The verdict turns on two things: (1) whether the literal event-type list satisfies the rule's requirement for launch/terminate/failure notifications, and (2) whether the unresolvable SNS topic ARN makes the configuration undecidable at analysis time.

Searched AWS docs for Auto Scaling notification types. The CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup NotificationConfiguration (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup-notificationconfiguration.html) and the Auto Scaling API reference for NotificationConfiguration both enumerate exactly five allowed values: autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH_ERROR, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE, autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATE_ERROR, and autoscaling:TEST_NOTIFICATION. TEST_NOTIFICATION is a separate, distinct value from all four instance lifecycle/error types; it is the value Auto Scaling uses to confirm the SNS wiring, not a subscription to any scaling event. There is no documented behavior by which specifying TEST_NOTIFICATION causes launch, terminate, or error events to be published, and the AWS CloudFormation walkthrough example of a properly notified ASG lists the four lifecycle/error types explicitly.

Because NotificationTypes here is stated literally and contains none of the four qualifying types, the deployed group publishes no launch, terminate, or failure notification. The intrinsic-exception path does not apply: the deployment-time input governs only the TopicARN destination, and every possible topic value yields the same outcome — no scaling-event notification is sent — so the breach is known at analysis time without resolving the input.
